subject: Mercantile Law
title: 9. Company Law — FPSC Heading: Companies Ordinance, 1984

segments.text: Company law governs incorporated business entities, their formation, constitutional documents, capital, management, meetings, accountability and winding up.

Use the FPSC conceptual headings but study them under the current Companies Act 2017. Understand separate legal personality, limited liability, company types, memorandum and articles, share capital, management organs, meetings, audit and winding-up/exit mechanisms.
Current principal company-law authority: Companies Act, 2017 and current SECP rules, regulations, amendments and schedules.

The FPSC syllabus heading historically refers to the Companies Ordinance, 1984, but Pakistan’s principal contemporary company-law framework is the Companies Act, 2017. SECP publishes the Act and later amendments and updated schedules, including schedule updates published in 2025–26. The syllabus heading should therefore be preserved for orientation while the current legal position is taught through the 2017 Act and current SECP instruments.
This is an important example of why the examination syllabus and current governing law must be read together rather than assuming that an older title remains controlling.

A company is an incorporated legal person distinct from its members. Formation requires compliance with the statutory incorporation process and constitutional documents. The memorandum sets fundamental corporate parameters, while articles regulate internal governance subject to the Act. Separate personality explains why company property is not simply shareholder property and why liability can be limited in recognized company forms.

Promoters arrange formation; directors manage or supervise corporate affairs within their duties; shareholders exercise member rights; the chief executive performs the management role defined by law and corporate governance; auditors provide independent assurance under applicable requirements.

blocks.text: Capital, disclosure, governance and winding up

segments.text: Shares represent membership/equity interests, while debentures generally represent debt obligations. Prospectus and disclosure rules protect investors by requiring legally specified information when securities are offered in relevant circumstances. Meetings and voting translate membership rights into corporate decisions.

Winding up is the legal process of bringing the company’s affairs to an end, realizing assets, settling liabilities and distributing any surplus according to law. It must be distinguished from ordinary insolvency distress, striking off, restructuring and voluntary business closure mechanisms.

items.text: Company law starts with separate legal personality:
incorporation creates an entity distinct from its members, with its own rights, liabilities and continuity subject to law.

Limited liability means members' financial exposure is limited according to the company's legal form and the law; it does not mean directors or members can never incur personal liability for their own unlawful conduct.

The memorandum contains foundational constitutional matters; articles regulate internal management and governance subject to statute. A prospectus concerns invitation and disclosure in relation to securities where legally applicable.
Governance can be mapped as members/shareholders, board of directors, chief executive and other officers, with auditors performing independent assurance functions under law.

Shares represent ownership interests; debentures are debt instruments. Meetings, resolutions, accounts, audit and winding up should be studied as parts of the company life-cycle under the current Companies Act framework.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not prepare the repealed Companies Ordinance as if it were the current general company statute. Preserve the FPSC heading, but study the concepts under current law as the source document correctly notes.

Prepare memorandum vs articles vs prospectus.
Use SECP’s current Act and rules for exact statutory detail.

segments.text: Company is a legal person distinct from members.
Memorandum defines foundational company matters; articles regulate internal governance subject to law.
Directors manage through board structures and owe statutory duties.
Winding up is a formal process for ending corporate existence/affairs.

Pakistan Code records Companies Ordinance 1984 as repealed by Act XIX of 2017. SECP currently publishes the Companies Act 2017 and its updated schedules. FPSC’s old syllabus heading is therefore retained only for alignment.
